                "headline": "Flood Watch issued October 31 at 2:11PM MDT until November 1 at 11:00PM MST by NWS Salt Lake City UT",
                "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...A portion of Utah, including the following areas, Castle\nCountry, San Rafael Swell, Bryce Canyon Country, Capitol Reef\nNational Park and Vicinity, Glen Canyon Recreation Area/Lake\nPowell, South Central Utah, Southern Mountains, Western\nCanyonlands, Lower Washington County and Zion National Park.\n\n* WHEN...From late tonight through Sunday evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, dry washes, slot canyons, and other low-lying and\nflood-prone locations such as slickrock areas and recent burn\nscars.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- Widespread moderate to at times heavy precipitation is expected\nacross much of southern, southeast and east central Utah\nbeginning late Saturday night, and continuing throughout the day\nSunday.\n\nMoist antecedent conditions from recent heavy rains will result\nin efficient and excessive runoff, allowing all area washes,\nstreams and rivers to run fast and high. Flood prone areas will\nlikely become inundated at times, and backcountry roads will\nlikely become impassable from this excessive runoff.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",

                "senderName": "NWS Albuquerque NM",
                "headline": "Flood Watch issued October 31 at 11:53AM MDT until November 2 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Albuquerque NM",
                "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of north central, northwest, and west central New\nMexico, including the following areas, in north central New Mexico,\nFar Northwest Highlands, Jemez Mountains, Northwest Highlands and\nTusas Mountains Including Chama. In northwest New Mexico, Chuska\nMountains and Northwest Plateau. In west central New Mexico, San\nFrancisco River Valley, Southwest Mountains, West Central\nHighlands, West Central Mountains and West Central Plateau.\n\n* WHEN...From late tonight through Monday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\nCreeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur\nin poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be\nflooded.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- Another round of widespread rainfall is expected Sunday into\nMonday with rainfall amounts generally between 1 and 2 inches\nnear and west of the Continental Divide, except near 3 inches in\nfavored upslope regions of the Tusas Mountains near Chama. This\nrainfall will occur over very saturated soils which will increase\nrunoff. These are also areas that are still recovering from the\nlast flood event. River rises are likely, but rises are not\nexpected to be as high as the last flood event. If river flooding\nmaterializes, it will likely continue into Monday evening.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
                "instruction": "You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood\nWarnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared\nto take action should flooding develop.",

                "instruction": "Onshore winds and above normal tides will combine to generate\nflooding of low areas along the shore.                 "description": "* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.\nFor the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents. For the\nHigh Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 7 feet\nexpected in the surf zone.\n\n* WHERE...Coastal portions of Saint Lucie and Martin Counties.\n\n* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 7 PM EST Sunday.\nFor the High Rip Current Risk, through late Monday night. Only isolated road closures are\nexpected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and\nlocalized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best\nswimmers away from shore into deeper water.",
                "instruction": "Onshore winds and above normal tides will combine to generate\nflooding of low areas along the shore. Do not drive around\nbarricades or through water of unknown depth. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and\nsigns.\n\nEntering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip\ncurrent, relax and float. Don't swim against the current.                 "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
                "senderName": "NWS Albuquerque NM",
